title: Epic: Certified Labeler — Hypercert Activity Quality Scorer with Hyperscan-style Dashboard
description:
## Goals
Build a Next.js labeler app that monitors org.hypercerts.claim.activity records on the AT Protocol network and labels DIDs based on how completely/carefully they fill out their hypercert activity claims. The system fights spam/test hypercerts by automatically scoring record completeness and applying tiered quality labels.

## Architecture
Two-process design sharing one codebase:
1. **Labeler process** (src/labeler/): Standalone Node.js process — Jetstream WebSocket consumer + @skyware/labeler LabelerServer + scoring engine. Listens for org.hypercerts.claim.activity creates, scores each record, applies quality labels to the author DID, and logs scored activities to SQLite.
2. **Next.js dashboard** (src/app/): Read-only web interface showing labeling stats, recent scored activities, and a filterable feed. Reads from the activity log SQLite DB.

## Label Tiers (4 labels, one per DID at a time)
- **high-quality** (✦, emerald) — Score ≥ 70/100. Well-documented, comprehensive activity claim.
- **standard** (●, blue) — Score 40-69. Adequate but could be more detailed.
- **draft** (◌, amber) — Score 15-39. Minimal information, work in progress.
- **likely-test** (⚠, rose) — Score 0-14 OR test content detected. Spam/placeholder data.

## Scoring (100 points total)
Analyzes org.hypercerts.claim.activity record fields: title quality (15), shortDescription quality (15), description presence+depth (20), image (10), workScope (10), contributor quality (15), locations (5), date range (5), rights (5). Test detection overrides: regex patterns for common test strings, duplicate title/description, gibberish.

## Design System
Hyperscan-inspired: Tailwind CSS v4 with OKLCH color space (hue 260 cool blue-slate). Syne display font, Outfit body, Geist system. Glassmorphism header, geometric background animation, staggered fade-in-up animations, noise texture. Monochrome base with semantic color accents.

## Tech Stack
Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript strict, Tailwind CSS v4, @skyware/labeler, @skyware/jetstream, better-sqlite3, pino, next-themes, prom-client.

## Key Constraints
- No shadcn/ui — hand-crafted components only
- No component library
- Code style: no semicolons, single quotes, 2-space indent
- The labeler process runs independently from Next.js (separate entry point)
- Dashboard is read-only (no auth, no writes)
- Activity log DB (activity-log.db) is separate from labeler's labels.db

title: Dashboard page — main landing page with stats and recent activity
description:
## Files

## What to do
Create the main dashboard page that shows labeling stats and recent scored activities.

### Component
```typescript
"use client"

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from "react"
import { StatsOverview } from "@/components/StatsOverview"
import { ActivityFeed } from "@/components/ActivityFeed"
import type { LabelStats, ActivityLogEntry } from "@/lib/types"

export default function DashboardPage()
```

### Layout
- `py-8 space-y-6 animate-fade-in-up`
- **Heading section** (`mb-2`):
  - Title: "certified labeler" in Syne font, text-2xl font-bold, lowercase
  - Subtitle: `text-sm text-muted-foreground mt-1` — "Monitoring hypercert activity quality across the hypersphere."
- **StatsOverview** section: fetched stats
- **Recent Activity** section:
  - Section header: `flex items-center justify-between mb-3`
    - Left: "Recent Activity" in `font-[family-name:var(--font-syne)] text-lg font-bold`
    - Right: Link to /feed — "View all →" in `text-xs text-muted-foreground hover:text-primary transition-colors`
  - ActivityFeed with last 10 activities

### Data Fetching
Use client-side fetch + useState + useEffect:

```typescript
const [stats, setStats] = useState<LabelStats | null>(null)
const [activities, setActivities] = useState<ActivityLogEntry[]>([])
const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true)

const fetchData = useCallback(async () => {
  try {
    const [statsRes, recentRes] = await Promise.all([
      fetch("/api/stats"),
      fetch("/api/recent?limit=10"),
    ])
    const statsData = await statsRes.json()
    const recentData = await recentRes.json()
    setStats(statsData.stats)
    setActivities(recentData.activities)
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Failed to fetch dashboard data:", error)
  } finally {
    setLoading(false)
  }
}, [])

useEffect(() => {
  fetchData()
  const interval = setInterval(fetchData, 30000) // Poll every 30s
  return () => clearInterval(interval)
}, [fetchData])
```

### Loading States
- While loading and no data: show skeleton/spinner for both stats and feed
- Stats skeleton: 4 rectangular `bg-secondary animate-pulse rounded-lg h-20` boxes in a row
- Feed skeleton: 3 rectangular `bg-secondary animate-pulse rounded-lg h-24` boxes stacked

### Empty State
When stats.total === 0: show a centered message below stats:
- "No activities scored yet."
- "The labeler process will analyze new org.hypercerts.claim.activity records as they appear on the network."
- Style: `text-center py-12 text-muted-foreground text-sm italic`

## Do not
- Do NOT use server components (this needs client-side polling)
- Do NOT implement infinite scroll (just show 10 with link to /feed)
- Do NOT add WebSocket/SSE real-time updates

title: Activity scoring engine — pure function to score org.hypercerts.claim.activity records
description:
## Files
- src/lib/scorer.ts (create)

## What to do
Create a pure, synchronous scoring function that analyzes an ActivityRecord and returns a ScoreResult.

### Main export
```typescript
import type { ActivityRecord, ScoreResult, ScoreBreakdown, LabelTier } from "./types"
import { TEST_PATTERNS, SCORE_THRESHOLDS } from "./constants"

export function scoreActivity(record: ActivityRecord): ScoreResult
```

### Scoring criteria (total 100 points)

1. **titleQuality** (0-15):
   - 0 if title.trim() matches any TEST_PATTERNS → add "title matches test pattern: {pattern}" to testSignals
   - 5 if title exists but length ≤ 10 chars
   - 10 if title > 10 chars
   - 15 if title > 30 chars AND contains at least one space (proper phrase)

2. **shortDescQuality** (0-15):
   - 0 if ≤ 10 chars or matches TEST_PATTERNS → add test signal
   - 5 if 10-50 chars
   - 10 if 50-150 chars
   - 15 if > 150 chars

3. **descriptionQuality** (0-20):
   - 0 if missing or empty
   - 5 if present but ≤ 100 chars
   - 10 if 100-500 chars
   - 15 if 500-1000 chars
   - 20 if > 1000 chars

4. **hasImage** (0-10):
   - 0 if missing/undefined
   - 10 if present (any truthy value with uri or file property)

5. **hasWorkScope** (0-10):
   - 0 if missing/undefined
   - 10 if present (either object with uri, or non-empty string)

6. **contributorQuality** (0-15):
   - 0 if missing or empty array
   - 5 if has ≥1 contributor
   - 10 if has ≥1 contributor WITH contributionWeight set
   - 15 if has ≥2 contributors with weights AND at least one has contributionDetails

7. **hasLocations** (0-5):
   - 0 if missing or empty array
   - 5 if has ≥1 location reference

8. **hasDateRange** (0-5):
   - 0 if neither startDate nor endDate
   - 2 if only one of startDate/endDate
   - 5 if both present

9. **hasRights** (0-5):
   - 0 if missing
   - 5 if present

### Test signal detection (checked BEFORE scoring)
Check these conditions and add string descriptions to testSignals[]:
- title.trim() matches any TEST_PATTERN → "title matches test pattern"
- shortDescription.trim() matches any TEST_PATTERN → "short description matches test pattern"
- title.trim().toLowerCase() === shortDescription.trim().toLowerCase() AND title.length < 50 → "title identical to short description"
- All characters in title are the same (e.g., "aaaa") → "title is repeated character"
- title.length < 3 → "title extremely short"

### Tier determination
```typescript
export function tierForScore(score: number, testSignals: string[]): LabelTier
```
1. If testSignals.length > 0, return "likely-test" (regardless of score)
2. Otherwise, find the tier in SCORE_THRESHOLDS where min ≤ score ≤ max
3. Default to "likely-test" if no match (should not happen with correct thresholds)

### Also export
```typescript
export function labelIdentifierForTier(tier: LabelTier): string
// Returns the identifier string, which is the same as the tier name
```

## Do not
- Do NOT access any database, network, or file system
- Do NOT import anything except from ./types and ./constants
- Do NOT use async functions — scoring is synchronous
- Do NOT import pino or any logger
acceptance_criteria:
1. scoreActivity({ title: "Mangrove Restoration Project in Madagascar — 2024 Phase 2", shortDescription: "Comprehensive tracking of a large-scale mangrove planting initiative spanning 150 hectares across three coastal sites, documenting community engagement and biodiversity outcomes.", description: "A".repeat(1200), image: { uri: "https://example.com/img.jpg" }, workScope: { uri: "at://did:plc:abc/org.hypercerts.helper.workScopeTag/123", cid: "abc" }, contributors: [{ contributorIdentity: "did:plc:a", contributionWeight: "50" }, { contributorIdentity: "did:plc:b", contributionWeight: "50", contributionDetails: "Lead researcher" }], locations: [{ uri: "at://x/y/z", cid: "c" }], startDate: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", endDate: "2024-12-31T00:00:00Z", rights: { uri: "at://x/y/z", cid: "c" }, createdAt: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }) returns tier "high-quality" with score ≥ 70
2. scoreActivity({ title: "test", shortDescription: "testing 123", createdAt: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }) returns tier "likely-test" with testSignals containing at least one entry
3. scoreActivity({ title: "My First Impact Claim", shortDescription: "A brief summary of my work", createdAt: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z" }) returns tier "draft" with score between 15-39
4. scoreActivity({ title: "Urban Garden Biodiversity Survey", shortDescription: "Measuring species richness in community gardens across Berlin. Collected data on pollinators, birds, and soil organisms over 6 months.", description: "Detailed methodology paragraph of about 200 chars covering our sampling approach and data collection", createdAt: "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", contributors: [{ contributorIdentity: "did:plc:x", contributionWeight: "100" }] }) returns tier "standard" with score between 40-69
5. All ScoreBreakdown fields are non-negative integers
6. testSignals is always an array (empty if no test signals)
7. totalScore equals the sum of all ScoreBreakdown field values
8. No async functions, no side effects, no imports beyond types+constants

title: Activity log database — SQLite schema and read/write functions
description:
## Files
- src/lib/db.ts (create)

## What to do
SQLite database using better-sqlite3 that stores scored activities for the dashboard. This is SEPARATE from the LabelerServer labels.db.

### Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activities (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  did TEXT NOT NULL,
  rkey TEXT NOT NULL,
  uri TEXT NOT NULL,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  score INTEGER NOT NULL,
  tier TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(tier IN ("high-quality", "standard", "draft", "likely-test")),
  breakdown TEXT NOT NULL,
  test_signals TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT "[]",
  labeled_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime("now")),
  UNIQUE(did, rkey)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activities_tier ON activities(tier);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activities_labeled_at ON activities(labeled_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_activities_did ON activities(did);
```

### Exports

```typescript
import Database from "better-sqlite3"
import { ACTIVITY_DB_PATH } from "./config"
import type { ActivityLogEntry, LabelStats, LabelTier } from "./types"

// Lazy-init singleton. Creates DB file + tables on first call.
export function getDb(): Database.Database

// Insert or replace (upsert on did+rkey). Does not throw on duplicates.
export function logActivity(entry: Omit<ActivityLogEntry, "id">): void

// Recent activities sorted by labeled_at DESC. Default limit=20, offset=0.
export function getRecentActivities(limit?: number, offset?: number): ActivityLogEntry[]

// Get activities filtered by tier. Sorted by labeled_at DESC.
export function getActivitiesByTier(tier: LabelTier, limit?: number, offset?: number): ActivityLogEntry[]

// Get total count (optionally filtered by tier)
export function getTotalCount(tier?: LabelTier): number

// Get aggregate statistics
export function getStats(): LabelStats
```

### getStats() implementation
```typescript
{
  total: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activities,
  byTier: {
    "high-quality": SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activities WHERE tier = "high-quality",
    "standard": ...,
    "draft": ...,
    "likely-test": ...,
  },
  last24h: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activities WHERE labeled_at > datetime("now", "-1 day"),
  last7d: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM activities WHERE labeled_at > datetime("now", "-7 days"),
}
```

### logActivity() implementation
Use INSERT OR REPLACE to handle duplicate (did, rkey) pairs. Map ActivityLogEntry fields to column names: breakdown → breakdown, testSignals → test_signals, labeledAt → labeled_at.

## Do not
- Do NOT use the same database file as LabelerServer labels.db

title: Score display components — ScoreBadge, ScoreCard, ScoreBreakdown
description:
## Files
- src/components/ScoreBadge.tsx (create)
- src/components/ScoreCard.tsx (create)
- src/components/ScoreBreakdown.tsx (create)

## What to do
Create the three visual components for displaying activity quality scores.

### ScoreBadge.tsx
"use client" component. Small inline badge showing the label tier.

```typescript
import type { LabelTier } from "@/lib/types"

interface ScoreBadgeProps {
  tier: LabelTier
  score?: number
  size?: "sm" | "md"
}
export function ScoreBadge({ tier, score, size = "sm" }: ScoreBadgeProps)
```

**Colors per tier:**
- high-quality: `bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700 border-emerald-200 dark:bg-emerald-500/10 dark:text-emerald-400 dark:border-emerald-500/20`
- standard: `bg-blue-50 text-blue-700 border-blue-200 dark:bg-blue-500/10 dark:text-blue-400 dark:border-blue-500/20`
- draft: `bg-amber-50 text-amber-700 border-amber-200 dark:bg-amber-500/10 dark:text-amber-400 dark:border-amber-500/20`
- likely-test: `bg-rose-50 text-rose-700 border-rose-200 dark:bg-rose-500/10 dark:text-rose-400 dark:border-rose-500/20`

**Label text per tier:** "✦ High Quality", "● Standard", "◌ Draft", "⚠ Likely Test"

**Size sm:** `text-[10px] px-2 py-0.5 rounded-full border font-medium`
**Size md:** `text-xs px-2.5 py-1 rounded-full border font-medium`

If score is provided, append " (87)" after the label text.

### ScoreCard.tsx
"use client" component. Card displaying a single scored activity.

```typescript
import type { ActivityLogEntry } from "@/lib/types"

interface ScoreCardProps {
  entry: ActivityLogEntry
  defaultExpanded?: boolean
}
export function ScoreCard({ entry, defaultExpanded = false }: ScoreCardProps)
```

**Layout:**
- Outer: `border border-border rounded-lg overflow-hidden bg-card transition-colors hover:bg-accent/30`
- **Header row** (`flex items-center justify-between px-3 py-2.5`):
  - Left: DID truncated to first 20 chars in `font-mono text-[11px] text-muted-foreground`
  - Right: Relative timestamp (e.g., "2m ago", "1h ago", "3d ago") in `text-[10px] text-muted-foreground/60`
- **Title row** (`px-3 pb-1`): `text-sm font-medium text-foreground truncate` showing entry.title
- **Score bar + badge row** (`flex items-center gap-2 px-3 pb-2.5`):
  - Score bar: `flex-1 h-1.5 rounded-full bg-secondary overflow-hidden` with inner div at width = score% colored by tier (emerald/blue/amber/rose with opacity)
  - ScoreBadge component with tier and score
- **Expandable breakdown**: Click card to toggle. When expanded, render ScoreBreakdown below with `px-3 py-2.5 border-t border-border/50` wrapper. Use useState for toggle. Animate with CSS grid trick: `grid transition-[grid-template-rows] duration-200 grid-rows-[0fr]` → `grid-rows-[1fr]` when expanded.

**Relative timestamp function:**
Calculate difference between now and entry.labeledAt. Show: "<1m ago", "Xm ago", "Xh ago", "Xd ago".

### ScoreBreakdown.tsx
Component showing detailed scoring criteria.

```typescript
import type { ScoreBreakdown as ScoreBreakdownType } from "@/lib/types"

interface ScoreBreakdownProps {
  breakdown: ScoreBreakdownType
  testSignals: string[]
}
export function ScoreBreakdown({ breakdown, testSignals }: ScoreBreakdownProps)
```

**Layout:** Vertical stack of criterion rows.

**Each criterion row** (`flex items-center gap-3 py-1`):
- Label: `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground w-28 shrink-0` — human-readable name
- Progress bar: `flex-1 h-1 rounded-full bg-secondary overflow-hidden` with inner div at width = (value/maxValue * 100)%
- Score text: `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground font-mono w-10 text-right` — "12/15"

**Criteria to display (label → field → max):**
1. "Title" → titleQuality → 15
2. "Summary" → shortDescQuality → 15
3. "Description" → descriptionQuality → 20
4. "Image" → hasImage → 10
5. "Work Scope" → hasWorkScope → 10
6. "Contributors" → contributorQuality → 15
7. "Locations" → hasLocations → 5
8. "Date Range" → hasDateRange → 5
9. "Rights" → hasRights → 5

**Progress bar colors:** Use the same tier-color logic based on value/maxValue ratio: ≥0.7 emerald, ≥0.4 blue, ≥0.15 amber, else rose.

**Test signals section:** If testSignals.length > 0, render below the criteria:
- `mt-2 p-2 rounded-md bg-rose-50 dark:bg-rose-500/10 border border-rose-200 dark:border-rose-500/20`
- Warning icon (inline SVG, small triangle with !) + "Test signals detected" in `text-[11px] font-medium text-rose-700 dark:text-rose-400`
- Each signal as a bullet: `text-[10px] text-rose-600 dark:text-rose-400/80`

## Do not
- Do NOT fetch any data (these are pure presentation components)
- Do NOT use framer-motion or any animation library
- Do NOT import from src/labeler/
- Do NOT use any icon library — inline SVGs only
acceptance_criteria:
1. ScoreBadge renders with correct colors for all 4 tiers (emerald/blue/amber/rose)
2. ScoreBadge shows score in parentheses when score prop is provided
3. ScoreCard displays DID (truncated), title, score bar, and badge
4. ScoreCard score bar width matches the score percentage
5. ScoreCard expands/collapses to show ScoreBreakdown on click
6. ScoreBreakdown shows all 9 criteria rows with labels, progress bars, and scores
7. ScoreBreakdown test signals section appears only when testSignals has entries
8. Relative timestamp shows correct human-readable time (e.g., "2m ago")
9. All components render correctly in both light and dark mode
10. No TypeScript errors — all props properly typed
